transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-09
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Elliot Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (CISO, Sandstone Health), Devon Park (Head of Infrastructure), Aisha Khan (App Sec), Ravi Patel (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick triage of recent PT findings, agreement on immediate patches, discussion of audit logs/KMS rotation, and next steps to validate fixes in staging.

00:00:00 Elliot Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have 54 minutes on the calendar. Quick intro, I'm Elliot, AE, and Priya is our security lead.
00:00:12 Priya Rao: Hi, hey all. We'll jump into the red team highlights then go into vuln mgmt and patch cadence.
00:00:20 Marta Lopez: Thanks. We only have the exec summary so far, was hoping to get the raw findings and what you think is immediate risk.
00:00:28 Elliot Chen: Totally. Priya, do you want to take the first pass?
00:00:31 Priya Rao: Sure. So the overall engagement was last week, red team surfaced eight medium-to-critical findings. There was one critical remote code exec path that depended on a misconfigured admin endpoint plus outdated dependency on route-handler 2.x — splashy, I know. The rest are mostly auth misconfigs and a couple of information exposures in auth tokens.
00:01:05 Devon Park: That RCE, can you be more specific? Which service, and is it reachable from public internet?
00:01:13 Priya Rao: It's the /internal-admin service behind the API gateway, it got exposed due to a path routing exception in our ingress rules. It was reachable from the corp VPN but not fully public — misrouting allowed the test agent to pivot. Transcription note: ingress was transcribed as 'in-grass' earlier in our internal notes, so apologies for that.
00:01:34 Ravi Patel: Ok, so that's within the VPC but reachable by users on VPN, that means our patch window needs to cover the internal subnet. We generally need two hours for deploy + smoke.
00:01:46 Aisha Khan: From app sec perspective, the issue also ties back to our CI job that skipped the lint step on the last deploy. We have a gating rule but it's not enforced for hotfix branches.
00:01:57 Priya Rao: Right, and that matches the SDLC pattern we flagged — missing enforcement on hotfix pipelines.
00:02:06 Marta Lopez: SOC 2 angle — we need to demonstrate the remediation steps and timeline for the auditors; can Redwood provide an exportable audit trail showing the reproduction and remediation validation?
00:02:18 Elliot Chen: Yes, we can. Priya, we can pull the request-level audit logs and a filtered KV-cache trace for the session window. It will include timestamps, actor IDs, and IP so you can attach to evidence.
00:02:31 Priya Rao: I'll export the runtime logs and produce a redacted bundle. Note that some service names might be anonymized in the export, and sometimes the auto transcript mislabels them — e.g., KV cache could be 'KV cash' in the transcript.
00:02:43 Marta Lopez: Great. Also curious about key management — one of the findings noted that some service secrets are using long-lived keys in our KMS project. We have a rotation policy but it hasn't been enforced in a few services.
00:02:55 Priya Rao: We recommend rotating service keys for the impacted services immediately and enabling automatic rotation where possible. Redwood supports KMS integration (we mentioned AWS KMS and GCP KMS) and we can provide guidance on key rotation windows and how to re-encrypt without downtime.
00:03:10 Devon Park: Does that mean we need a maintenance window for re-encryption? We try to avoid any full restarts for high-throughput services.
00:03:17 Elliot Chen: In most cases you can do staged rekeying: new key encrypts new writes while existing reads still use the old key until TTL expires. Priya, we had an internal doc on staged rekeying — can we link that?
00:03:29 Priya Rao: Yup, I'll attach the doc. In this call I'll also note that if you're on our private deployment (VPC) we can coordinate with your SREs to ensure KMS access is configured for minimal blast radius.
00:03:41 Aisha Khan: On RBAC and SSO — the red team exploited a mis-scoped role binding that allowed token introspection by a non-privileged service account. We use SAML SSO via Okta — our mappings for groups to roles are sometimes stale. Do you have recommendations for periodic role reviews?
00:03:58 Priya Rao: Yes, implement quarterly RBAC audits plus automated membership sync with SSO group claims. Redwood also emits fine-grained audit logs for token issuance and token introspection events, which can be routed to your SIEM.
00:04:11 Ravi Patel: How granular are those logs? We need to feed them into Splunk with a schema that includes actor, action, resource, outcome — ideally with request_id for traceability.
00:04:21 Priya Rao: We emit structured JSON logs with those fields; sometimes field names differ between environments, so we'll share a sample schema.
00:04:30 Marta Lopez: For SOC 2 evidence, auditors often ask for a sample of SSO mapping reviews and the audit logs around role changes. Would Redwood sign an attestation that logs are complete for the time range?
00:04:42 Elliot Chen: We can provide a signed extract and metadata about retention policies; for legal attestation we typically route requests to our security team and provide the export under an NDA. I'll note that as a follow-up.
00:04:55 Devon Park: On patch cadence — we usually do monthly security patches plus emergency hotfixes. Given these findings, is a faster cadence recommended?
00:05:03 Priya Rao: For exposed auth misconfigs and dependencies with public CVEs, we recommend immediate hotfix plus moving to biweekly security pulls for critical CVEs. Also, improving SCA policy enforcement in CI would reduce recurrence.
00:05:18 Aisha Khan: Can Redwood run a quick dependency scan on our image in staging? We want to validate the fix before going to prod.
00:05:24 Priya Rao: We can run an image dependency baseline scan and return a delta report. We'll need a short-lived access token or you can upload the SBOM to our portal.
00:05:32 Elliot Chen: I'll add that to action items — Priya to run the scan once they provide the SBOM.
00:05:38 Devon Park: About data residency: a couple of services have datasets that must remain in EU region for compliance. Any export bundles must not cross region. Can Redwood guarantee region-scoped exports?
00:05:51 Priya Rao: Yes, if you're on our Dedicated or Private deployment you can configure export endpoints to the EU region only. For hosted accounts we tag data residency and provide region-restricted exports; we'll confirm specifics in the follow-up doc.
00:06:05 Marta Lopez: Great. There was also a question about long-term retention of audit logs — auditors asked for 12 months for certain events. What's Redwood's retention policy?
00:06:14 Elliot Chen: By default hosted audit logs are retained for 90 days; we offer extended retention add-ons (12 months, multi-year) as an enterprise configuration. For Private you control retention. We'll include retention options in the follow-up.
00:06:28 Ravi Patel: On the remediation verification — once we patch, how do we validate? Do you run a regression check or will we run an internal pen test?
00:06:37 Priya Rao: We recommend a two-step validation: Redwood can do a focused validation test (the same checks the red team used) in staging, and then you can run an internal or third-party re-test for assurance. We'll share the test vectors.
00:06:50 Aisha Khan: One of the medium findings related to token leakage in logs — our logging config needs to scrub auth headers. Can Redwood provide guidance for log scrubbing patterns?
00:06:59 Priya Rao: Yes, we have example log processors and regex patterns to strip sensitive headers and PII before they hit the central logging pipeline. I'll share the snippets.
00:07:08 Devon Park: Are there any known regressions introduced by the hotfix we should watch for?
00:07:12 Priya Rao: The main risk is session invalidation when rotating keys and gating role binding changes; we'll recommend a staged rollout and a fallback route back to the previous service image. Redwood supports automatic fallback policy if health checks fail.
00:07:26 Elliot Chen: Ok, let's walk through immediate timeline — who can own the hotfix deployment?
00:07:31 Devon Park: SRE team can take it, I'll coordinate the window. Generally Tuesday 01:00 UTC for our maintenance.
00:07:37 Marta Lopez: For auditors we need remediation timeline in writing — can Redwood produce a one-page remediation plan with dates?
00:07:43 Elliot Chen: Yes — Priya will draft a remediation plan itemizing critical/ high/medium findings with owners and dates.
00:07:49 Priya Rao: I'll draft and share the spreadsheet. Also note: sometimes our auto transcript mislabels service names; please cross-check the service list in the spreadsheet with your internal inventory.
00:07:59 Ravi Patel: Quick question on rates: if we need Redwood to run multiple verification tests and provide extended log retention, what's the procurement route? Is that add-on billing or part of enterprise contract?
00:08:11 Elliot Chen: For customers on enterprise we can add retention and verification hours as contractual line items; I'll pull pricing and attach it. If you want to engage ad-hoc, we can do SOW for the red/validation runs.
00:08:23 Devon Park: Competitor question: we had previously evaluated ConvergeShield and liked their offline analysis tooling; how does Redwood's validation compare?
00:08:32 Priya Rao: Redwood focuses on runtime replay and structured audit traces tied to request_id — we aim to provide reproducible validation vs purely static offline analysis. Both have value; we'll share a comparison note.
00:08:44 Marta Lopez: Anything else?
00:08:46 Elliot Chen: I'll recap next steps: send redacted pen-test report and remediation spreadsheet, Priya exports logs and runs dependency scan when SBOM is provided, Sandstone confirms patch window and immediate endpoints, schedule follow-up technical deep dive week of Apr 20.
00:09:02 Marta Lopez: Sounds good. Thanks.
00:09:05 Devon Park: Thanks everyone.
00:09:07 Priya Rao: Thanks all.

(Transcript continues with Q&A and some cross talk; portions abridged.)

End of call.
